utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning to everyone. May we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Joanna Korner, Alex Demirdjian, and Crispian Smith for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, Eugene O'Sullivan, and Ms. Tatjana Savic appearing for the Stanisic Defence this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Dragan Krgovic and Aleksandar Aleksic appearing for Zupljanin Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. And I gather there is no reason to delay the return of the witness to the stand. Mr. Usher, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just one thing, Your Honour. I was notified that 1D469, which was MFI'd due to a revised translation, the double negation in the document, the new -- the revised translation has been uploaded so the document can be de-MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yeah, so ordered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good morning to you, sir. You may be seated. And before Mr. Zecevic resumes, I remind you you're still on your oath. Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Bjelosevic. I would like to take a look now at P813, tab 226. Mr. Bjelosevic, you can also see it on the screen in front of you. It's not a long document; only one page. Do you see it? This is a document dated the 17th of August, 1992. It comes from the Ministry of the Interior of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It was delivered to all Security Services Centres, rather, to the chiefs personally. At the bottom, we can see typed minister of the interior, Mico Stanisic, a signature, and a stamp. Have you received this document? What is it about? And do you recognise the signature? Can you comment on it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise the signature and the document. This related to the meeting in Trebinje on the 20th of August, and it said what we had to prepare for the meeting. As for the signature, it was signed by Petar Vujicic on the authority of the minister of the interior. Petar Vujicic was the chief of the analytical department.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you receive that document?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bjelosevic, did you attend this collegium in Trebinje?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we take a look at P163, which is tab 94.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is a summary from the MUP management working group meeting held on the 20th of August, 1992, in Trebinje. On page 4, your contribution to the discussion is recorded. In e-court, it's page 5, but the pagination on the paper is 4. Please take a look at this. It begins on this page and then goes over to the following page. So they are pages 5 and 6, or 4 and 5. Could you comment on what you said on this meeting and whether this summary records everything that you said at this meeting, as far as you can remember?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, we need page 6 in English. Or, rather, 6 and 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Have you read it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm about to finish. I read it. This is what I was saying at the meeting, and these are the problems that I described at the time. I also tried to describe some of them in my testimony here. The situation was, indeed, chaotic. I wish to emphasise what happened after the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was declared and the JNA withdrew from our territories. Some of the units, or, more precisely, parts of some units from that point on, began to act independently and out of control, which means that the hierarchy and the structure that existed within the JNA disappeared. The Army of Republika Srpska did not manage to take everything over and the command chains were not established yet, which means that there were problems of this kind with various groups who would enter the town during the night. And that's the essence of what I was saying. Yes, there was an increase in crime, desertion. That's about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me, this meeting, as well as the meeting on the 11th of July, were they both held in two sessions, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was the same. I think that the minister presided over the meeting, and then when there was a possibility to do so, for instance, to take certain chiefs of certain lines of work, for instance, public security, or state security, or crime prevention, then they spoke about their specific problems separately, and then they managed to reach certain agreements in relation to their line of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, do you remember whether any conclusions were made at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. First, there was the introduction by the minister, then a discussion. And then, at the end, as far as I can remember, some conclusions were made, and those conclusions were obligatory for everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's page 10 in e-court although the page itself bears number 9. I think that it's page 11 in English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, those are the conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you remember the conclusions as well? They run to four pages. There are nine items in conclusions.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Later on we also received this document. All the centres received it, and I remember that we received it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you take a look at page 15 in e-court, in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assume that it's page 17 in English, or 18. Also, the subsequent pages. On page 15 in e-court, the last paragraph, and in English -- no, this is not the right page. Can we have the following page. One more page. Can we turn one more page in English. Excuse me, one more page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, here can you see conclusions that were made by the public security department and formulated by Cedo Kljajic. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see from these conclusions that a lot of what we discussed on the 11th of July was transformed into a binding conclusion here. Maybe you remember that they talked about the problem of the official ID because it was misused on a large scale. There were stations of reserve police where there were forms, empty forms, and then they would take them, fill them in and give them to members of the military and others. And now I see that they are talking about how to solve this problem here. Especially interesting here is the following: Because of the complexity of the problems, the help should be extended in a particularly careful way with a very detailed preparation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the following page in e-court, both in Serbian and English.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do go on.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: War Presidencies and various other organs often requested the police to do this or to do that, and some of those requests were contrary to the laws and the regulations regulating the work of the MUP organs at the time. One of my colleagues highlighted this problem in one of the conclusions related to that, saying that such requests should be responded to in a very careful manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you maybe comment on the conclusion numbered with number 3?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Since the subordination system was in chaos, and we also found that when we visited our stations, and our colleagues from the field also highlighted this problem, one of the conclusions was that the subordination, as the basic principle of the command structure, should be implemented at all levels of the organisation and that the direction and management of work should be done only in accordance with this hierarchical structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now take a look at 211D1, tab 96.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, this document is dated the 24th of August, 1992. Comes from the CSB Doboj. It says here: "Plan approved by chief of the centre, Andrija Bjelosevic." Can you confirm that this is your document and tell us whether you received this plan of visit, and what is it all about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the meeting with the minister and senior officials in Trebinje, after I returned, I had a meeting with my associates. So we decided to make this plan of visits. The chiefs of the police were involved in that because they were very experienced people, and can you see here that this lists the dates of visits to certain stations. After this plan was made and signed by these two chiefs, inspectors, I approved it, and it was indeed realised. They did go to visit to those stations. If you remember yesterday, I mentioned that after the visit, they realised that there was a number of irregularities, for instance, in Samac, and after that we attempted to solve those problems. Mostly by replacing the chief in Samac. But, at the time, we couldn't do that. But, anyway, in order to clarify this, this meeting and these conclusions were the starting point for us to go into the field, visit those stations, and try to implement the conclusions from the meeting. This is one of the documents on the basis of which we did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, just one more comment in relation to this document. This visit and everything else that is referred to in the plan, is that instructional supervision, as it is called?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is what it says, that certain instructions would be provided. As for more drastic irregularities, certain measures were envisaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you say certain measures were envisaged, what measures do you mean?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean measures that are envisaged in the rules on disciplinary responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D505, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document that I wish to show you is 1D57, tab 98. This is a dispatch of the ministry of the RS. The date is the 24th of August. It is signed by the minister, Mr. Mico Stanisic. There is something handwritten on the top of the page. There's a name and surname in the corner. There's a number as well. Tell me, are you familiar with this document? Have you received it? And did you act in accordance with it? Or could you give us your comment in respect of this document.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that we received this document. We did act in accordance with it. We asked stations for information from their respective territories. We dealt with the information received, and we responded to this document, as requested, according to all of these questions. I do not recognise the handwriting, though, on the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document that I wish to show you is 1D64. That is tab 104. Sir, this is an order of the ministry dated the 6th of September, 1992. It is signed by the minister. There's a stamp there as well. Again, there's something handwritten on the top of the page. I don't know whether you are aware of what that was. Again, my same question: Have you received this document? Do you remember acting in accordance with it, if you did receive it? What can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we received this document, this order. It comes from the Ministry of the Interior. It is signed by Minister Stanisic; I recognise his signature. What is handwritten here on top of the page, I don't know. But I see it says "Kekic" and then "In records." I don't know. But I see that obviously it has been kept for the records. I remember the order. This was the minister's reaction to what was happening on the ground. He vested his own authority in this. He wanted people on the ground to act in accordance with regulations. You can see that that is what the document says here, that people should act in accordance with the ZKP, the Law on the Interior, and so on. Everything else as stated in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, are you familiar with this decree of the government of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina on the compulsory hand-over of war booty to war reserves?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that decree.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In point 3, this document refers to a decree. Is that the decree?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's it. And it was published in the Official Gazette, as stated here, and we received that Official Gazette with that decree.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document that I would like you to comment upon is tab 232. It is document 1D432.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 2, please. Page 2 of the document itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a decision of the Assembly of the Serb Municipality of Doboj. It is signed by the president of the Serbian Assembly. It is stamped as well. The date is the 23rd of July, 1992. Could you please tell us whether you are familiar with this decision, what it refers to, who signed it, and, generally speaking, your comment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember this document. Indeed, there was this propaganda in the media to the -- I mean, in this way, as is written here, that this was a torture ground and so on. And I know that a German journalist came with a TV crew to check those allegations, and I remember this decision. I remember that this decision was made, and it is binding on the public security station as well, that they should keep special records of all approvals issued on the basis of this order or this decision. Because of these rumours and because of this propaganda in the media, I also asked the chief of the station to write a memo about people who were moving out; who was moving out, what was their gender, their age, who was moving out in general, and how many people were moving out. I remember this decision of Mr. Ljubicic. At the time, he was president of the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You say that this German journalist came with a TV crew to check these allegations. It seems to me that a few days ago you said that a book was published and that you received it. Am I wrong? Or is that correct? A book written by that journalist?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. He wrote a book. He visited other areas as well. Not only Doboj. I think there's a reference to Doboj on some 14 or 15 pages. "Serbien muss Sterben" is the title of the book, and it was translated to me as "Serbia Must Die." We do have a translation of that book into Serbian. He explains why he gave such a tendencious title to the book. It was on account of this propaganda in the media that was directed against Serbia and the Serb people and so on. So this is his take on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Have you read the book? If so, did that journalist confirm in that book the --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't think so. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D433. Can we have a look at that document, please. Tab 231.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the document. This is a permit allowing a person to travel abroad. It was signed by the president of the Assembly of the Municipality of Doboj, Mr. Drago Ljubicic. You see who it pertains to, Ismet Kreho, an ethnic Muslim. This document allows him to travel to Barcelona and so on. There were other documents like this that were issued by the municipal authorities as permits for persons to travel. Now that we're on the subject, during a certain period of time, there was a person from the ICRC that I can recall. I think this person's name was Barbara. She came to Doboj often. She used to come to see me as well, and she dealt with such issues precisely, making it possible for certain persons to travel, providing them with transportation, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, this document, it is signed by the president of the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the president of the Municipal Assembly, Drago Ljubicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What are the organs that issued such permits?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to tell you that there were different organs that issued them, starting with the president of the municipality, then the Red Cross in some cases. As far as I can remember, the military commands issued such permits as well. It seems that it depended on who addressed who, asking for a permit. That's the only explanation I seem to be able to give.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let us look at document 215D1, tab 107.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have page 2; and then, after that, page 3. I mean the Serbian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, this is a document of the CSB of Doboj. The 8th of September, 1992, is the date. On the second page, it says chief of CSB, Andrija Bjelosevic. It is sent to the public security station in Doboj. Could you please confirm whether this is your document. And could you explain to us in detail what it was that you were asking for in this document, and why?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document of the CSB. I signed it. I did ask for this information from the public security station in Doboj. It is precisely because of all of these different rumours about who was moving out and why and for what reason. I thought that the matter should be discussed seriously and that it was indispensable to collect proper information that would show us what the picture actually was. And it is only then that we could make certain conclusions in that respect. So that is the document in which I requested that information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, to whom was this request sent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The CSB sent it to the public security station in Doboj, because they are the ones who have the records about citizens in the territory of the municipality of Doboj, or, rather, the area of the public security station of Doboj. They had a service that covered the entire town, or, rather, the entire territory that was within the then-municipality of Doboj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And what about the other SJBs in the Doboj area? Were they also given this request?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand. What other public security services? It is sent to the station. You can see from the heading, it says: "Public security station, Doboj."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I may of assistance, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bjelosevic, the question was as follows: Did you send a memo of this nature to other public security stations in your area?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Only to the Doboj SJB.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And why only to the Doboj SJB?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because -- because in that area, there were very many rumours, especially those broadcast in the media. There were a lot of stories circulating, and I wanted to establish the actual situation and to do something about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you say "in that area," are you referring to the Doboj municipality territory?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. To the Doboj municipality within the boundaries that existed at the time. I have already spoken about the fact that it was a smaller territory in relation to the pre-war territory of the municipality, that we already had Doboj east, Doboj south area, and now I'm referring to the territory which was under the effective control of the then-Serbian authorities of the Doboj municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Did you receive this information from the public security station?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know to what extent that information was accurate at the time; but, yes, they provided information to me, and I know that we analysed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And what was the end result of that analysis of yours? What did the analysis show, if you can explain, please?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first effect we established was that population of all ethnicities was moving out of the Doboj municipality. The other thing that was important was that there were some illegal departures which had not been reported to anyone. People simply left without notifying anyone. Third fact was that the age of people leaving was quite diverse, and one of the features was that it wasn't as portrayed by the media. It wasn't in that scope, and it wasn't done in the manner as portrayed by the media. I'm now referring to the media in the neighbouring areas, to Radio Tesanj and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unless there are objections, I tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D506, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 1D261, which is tab 114.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, the previous document we have just commented upon was dated the 8th of September. The one that we are looking at now is the document of the CSB, dated the 12th of September. It was sent to the Doboj public security station. It's an order. And in the bottom right corner, it says: "Chief of the Centre, Andrija Bjelosevic." Would you please confirm whether this is your document? Do you remember it? And why was it sent, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the document of the Doboj CSB. I signed it. It was sent to the public security station, and at the end of the document, I state that the chief of the SJB is responsible for implementation of the order. As you can see in the preamble of the order, very often people talked about what had happened in town during the night. There were frequent cases of certain groups coming in during the night, breaking into people's apartment, looting their property, mistreating people. Some people were even taken somewhere. And up until that time, the public security station did not inform the centre about any of these events, given that the witnesses described the events -- the eye-witnesses described these events in very unclear terms. For example, they would very often say they wore dark camouflage uniforms. And the problem was that, at the time, there was no electric power, and at night it was difficult for people to tell apart the camouflage uniforms and blue uniforms, and so on. Let me just mention that the phones were not operational because there was no electricity, and the batteries used for the telephone exchange were simply too old and not operational, so the phones didn't work. Therefore, timely information, timely notification, simply did not exist. This is why I asked that the public security station, via their patrols, collect information and also collect information from their crime prevention service to compile it, put it together in a document, and send it to the CSB.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Would you please remind us who was the chief of the public security station in Doboj at the time?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, it was Obren Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was this order of yours complied with?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in the terms contained in the order. They did something concerning the crime prevention work, but not as requested in the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You told us in the last sentence of your order, you say that the chief of the SJB is personally responsible for this?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what you can read in the last sentence of the order: "The chief of the SJB is personally responsible to me for the implementation of this order." And perhaps it might be important to mention, now that we're speaking about this, the following. In my personal discussions with the chief of the station, I tried to clarify certain matters, and very often he would reply to me in a short-tempered way. He would say to me, You see that the war is on, that everybody carries a rifle, they will kill me, they will kill you. So I had a feeling that he lived in a great deal of fear, that he was quite anxious. It is true that the times were quite chaotic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Since you say that this order was not complied with, did you do something about it? Did you undertake any measures?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After this, I called him several times. We talked, and I asked him to either ensure law and order in the territory of his municipality or else I would ask that he would be replaced, which is what I did later. And let me just tell you that this was not the only reason for my action. In the reserve forces, there were some individuals and groups that simply did not belong to the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We will go back to this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 220D1, tab 112.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, sir, this document is dated 12th of September, 1992, signed -- or, rather, typed Andrija Bjelosevic, signature, seal, and this was sent to the Ministry of the Interior of the Serbian Republic. At the top, we see handwritten text. There's a name and a date. Would you please tell us whether this is your handwriting, whether this is your document, whether it was sent to the ministry, and what do you know about this, and what do you know about this handwriting?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document from the Doboj CSB. I signed it. It was addressed to the Ministry of the Interior. And in that document, I asked that Official Gazette copies be sent to us for the use of the centre and also stations in the territory of the Doboj CSB, so that we could have in our possession the regulations that had been passed and so that we could act in accordance with those regulations. Initially all of the federal regulations had been taken over, and then following that, certain decrees were passed, instructions, directives and so on, so it was necessary for us to have all that body of new regulations so that we could comply with them. I see the date at the top, 18th of September, which means that this is something that was written in the MUP seat, in the MUP headquarters, in their records department. I don't recognise the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether the MUP acted upon your request?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After a certain period of time, we received a number of copies of the Official Gazette of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, as it was known at the time, with the regulations that had been published until that time. And then I organised that these copies be distributed to the stations so that each station would have Official Gazettes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unless there are objections, I would like this to be admitted please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Why do we need this, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I believe it's -- it's important and very relevant, the fact that -- that the CSB and the SJBs were lacking the actual knowledge of the laws at the time. And, yes, that they were requesting -- it shows the conditions under which they were working, and I think it's important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Probably similar request for pencils around the same time. I mean, all of this is -- it's merely a -- I mean, how does it assist, having this piece of paper added to the pile?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I think it depicts the situation in which the SJBs and the CSB Doboj worked at the time. And I think it is very relevant because -- because, based on that, the certain standards can be applied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: But we have the testimony of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honours, I just ... thank you. [Interpretation] The next document, 219D1, tab 113.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this document is dated 12th of September, 1992. It was sent to public security station, signed by Andrija Bjelosevic. Would you please clarify to us -- or, rather, first confirm whether this is your document, whether you sent it out as the CSB, and do you remember what this pertains to, since, unfortunately, we do not have the government decision mentioned here?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise the document, emanating from the CSB Doboj. I signed it, and it was sent as a cover letter with the enclosed document to the public security stations that existed at the time within the jurisdiction of the Doboj CSB. And attached to this cover letter was the government decision, specifying persons and facilities that would require special security measures, and also an extract from the directive on the scope, method of security provided to certain persons and facilities, important public events and so on. This was sent to all of the SJBs out there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If you remember, can you give us some additional explanations. What specific persons, what facilities, and so on.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. These were persons -- or, rather, functions. Members of the Presidency, president of the government, of the Assembly, members of delegations of foreign states that visited the territories of the then-Serbian republic, as well as the facilities where they had their headquarters. In addition to that, there were separate rules about providing security to public gatherings and mass gatherings in general. The rules specified the various levels of security that had to be applied if those gatherings were attended by certain dignitaries, and so on and so forth. That's the essence of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm not even going to try to propose this document because I assume that the position of the Trial Chamber will be the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I just have a query, if I may, while the document's on the screen, which I don't think the witness explained. It is addressed apparently to public security stations from 1 to 7. I don't know whether that has any specific meaning or relevance.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you explain this, Mr. Bjelosevic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes public security stations are listed by their names. Sometimes it says here "to all." Sometimes it says from number 1 to number 7. But the essence of the matter is that all of them were included.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you maybe then list all those stations.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Public security station Doboj, Modrica, Samac, Derventa, Maglaj -- yes, Maglaj stationed in Jablanica. And then Teslic and Petrovo. Those are the stations that comprised the Security Services Centre in Doboj at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to take a look at 222D1, tab 116.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, would you allow me to add one more sentence in relation to this?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Certainly. Go on.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Although at the time the public security station Teslic was within the Security Services Centre in Doboj, the Law on the Interior actually envisaged that it should have been a part of the Security Services Centre in Doboj. So every time that we would forward any documents to any other stations we would always also send those documents to them. I just wanted to add this so that it would be clear why this particular station is also included in here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But, Mr. Bjelosevic, I think you told us yesterday that there were nine SJBs under the Doboj CSB's jurisdiction; Brod, Derventa, Odzak, Samac, Modrica, Doboj, Tesanj, Teslic, and Maglaj. These were the nine SJBs that you mentioned yesterday, and I suppose this is what triggered the Prosecution's questions as to why there were only seven mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me explain. Before the war, the territory of the Security Services Centre Doboj covered nine stations, and I already mentioned them. They were Brod, Odzak, Samac, Derventa, Maglaj, Modrica, Doboj, Teslic, and Tesanj. In the period that we are discussing now, in relation to the previous document, I already said it several times, and I'm going to emphasise it once again, things changed. So at one moment, Security Services Centre in Doboj did not have power over any other station except the Doboj station. That was the situation at a certain point in time. And then things changed. And now, when we talk about the period in September, then we are talking about the stations that I just enumerated. So I just wanted to add one short explanation related to Teslic and the public security station in Teslic because it was a specific situation. The Municipal Assembly in Teslic on the 6th of April, 1992, decided that this municipality and all the organs of the municipality should be associated with the Autonomous Region of Krajina. So the public security station there did that. However, the law remained the same. There were no changes in the law. So whenever I sent any of our documents to our public security stations, the public security stations covered by the centre in Doboj, I would also send those documents to public security station in Teslic because that was the law, while, in actual fact, they actually functioned as part of the CSB in Banja Luka. That's just what I wanted to explain here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this clarification, and I apologise for not having picked this up from your testimony. So if Doboj originally had nine SJBs under its jurisdiction, and if Teslic then, on 6 April 1992, decided to join the ARK in Banja Luka, then that would leave eight SJBs under this jurisdiction, and that brings me back to the number of SJBs mentioned in your letter here. Only -- where there are only seven. I apologise, but I don't know if this is important, but -- but it may be.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is up to you to decide whether it's important. I am certainly prepared to explain it once again so that it is clear to everybody. Maybe I should do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So now we know the situation related to Teslic. The situation deteriorated in April, the security situation in particular. In my first days of testimony here, I already explained what happened to the public security station Brod. I said that practically from March onwards, this station was associated with the police administration in Slavonski Brod. Later on, with the barricades and guards, and also with the establishment on the front line, all communication with the public security station in Odzak was severed. Public security station in Derventa was occupied by -- well, I don't know if I can really call it Territorial Defence because I already told you there were some volunteers involved. Anyway, this station also left our jurisdiction, the Doboj centre jurisdiction. Sometime mid-April, public security station in Samac, together with the whole municipality, was taken over by the military forces. Modrica had by that time already been cut off from Doboj. There was fighting around Modrica and two or three times Modrica went from one hand to another pair of hands, another forces. And sometime in April, we even received a dispatch saying, "We are not going to obey CSB Doboj and we are not going to communicate with Doboj at all." Did you get the picture now? At a certain moment, that was the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, sir, this was very illustrative. Back to you, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Just one moment, please. Mr. Bjelosevic, I hope I'm not adding to the confusion that I'm trying to clarify. There were nine SJBs before the war; seven in September -- the seven you mentioned. Yes? Three from before the war are not under CSB Doboj anymore. That's Brod, Odzak, and Tesanj -- no, Tesanj, right? So that makes six? And there's one that was not there before the war, Petrovo. Okay. Can you -- where is Petrovo? Where does it come from? Is it another name for something that existed before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The territory of Petrovo municipality used to belong to the Gracanica municipality before the war, and part of it was Lukavac municipality. And then Petrovo municipality was established. It means that it was a completely new municipality. It did not exist before. And then sometime in August, in Petrovo municipality, in accordance with the Law of Administrative Division of the Territories, a public security station was established as well, from scratch. New municipality, new station. To clarify one thing about Maglaj. The town of Maglaj and the greater part of the territory of that municipality was controlled by Muslim and Croat forces. One part, towards Ozren and Doboj, was then the part of the territory where some Serb policemen who had left Maglaj formed an area that was administratively within the Maglaj municipality but it was controlled by Serbian forces. So, at that time, there was a public security station Maglaj headquarter in the town of Maglaj itself, and then there was also a Maglaj station that was controlled by the Security Services Centre in Doboj. And then, later on, when the territories to the north and to the east were liberated, Derventa was liberated, and then the public security station in Derventa was re-established. In Modrica also the public security station was re-established. In Odzak, there was military rule, as well as in Brod, but, later on, things also started functioning there, and public security stations were established there as well. So situation changed with time, depending on who controlled the territory, which elements of our services functioned. And now, if we talk about the relevant period of time, relevant for this particular document, at that point in time, we had the seven stations that I listed earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Just to be complete, what happened to Tesanj station at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tesanj? Public security station in Tesanj remained within the jurisdiction of the then-Muslim forces, and even today, it's within the Federation. And that goes for the whole territory and municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see the time. Perhaps this would be an appropriate moment to take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. There are certain matters with which the Chamber intends to deal with during the break, so I'm going to extend the break to a half-hour. So we would resume, well, at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: While the witness is being escorted back to the stand, the Chamber has a brief ruling to deliver which is as follows. The Chamber has considered the motion of the Defence of Mico Stanisic regarding the testimony of the witness Christian Nielsen, and the submissions in response of the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I just -- sorry to interrupt. Can I remind Your Honours that both the Defence motion and our response were filed confidentially.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. So we go into private session. Thank you, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please continue, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown document 222D1, tab 116.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, this is a document of the Doboj CSB signed by Chief of the Centre, Andrija Bjelosevic, submitted to the public security stations of the area. The document consists of three pages. On pages 2 and 3, we find the attachments to this letter. So could you please confirm whether this is a document of yours, who it was sent to, and for what reason?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document of the CSB Doboj. It was sent to the public security stations, in order to provide a review of all the orders and instructions that were issued by the Doboj CSB and the Ministry of the Interior. All of that was listed here and submitted to the stations so that they could use that and act in accordance with these orders and instructions that had been issued. I think that this became necessary when we realised, during the course of a meeting, that not all stations had these documents. Now why did they not have them? We saw how some of these public security stations were being established. Some were established earlier, some were established later. Some received all the documents that had been issued immediately, and others did not, so then we realised that everyone needed to be provided with a full set of documents. That was the purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Were the stations duty-bound to carry out these instructions in their work?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. They were duty-bound to do that so the very word itself, "order," makes it binding. And instructions as well. They are thereby instructed as to how they should behave.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: During those instructional supervisions, or inspections, was it being established whether these orders and instructions were being abided by?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The work of the service is regulated by the Law on the Interior and bylaws that are derived from that law. These bylaws regulate certain areas more specifically. Therefore, these instructions are binding as well and that they must be complied with. The supervision that was carried out, regardless of whether it was carried out by inspectors coming from the headquarters of the MUP or inspectors from the CSB, was precisely aimed at that. Namely, establishing whether public security stations acted in accordance with the law and these bylaws that were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Again, my refrain, Mr. Zecevic, why do we need this to -- which merely substantiates the -- what one would expect to have been the routine decisions of the administration in this situation, which -- to which the witness has testified?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think it's relevant because in the next two pages is the list of the instructive acts and the orders from the Ministry of Interior of RS. And it shows that up until second part of September, some of the SJBs in the territory of this CSB were not in possession of these instructive acts or orders, and I think that -- that's -- in our opinion that is very relevant.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I'm not objecting to the document but I don't think comments such as that it shows up to the second part of September, some of the SJBs in the territory were not in possession of these instructions, is a proper comment. It actually doesn't say that at all. It just says here they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, we have the witness's testimony to that effect, and it's up to the Trial Chamber to decide what was said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We'll admit it as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D507, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown document 230D1, tab 139.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, while that is happening perhaps I better just correct the transcript, page 30, line 9. It shows question, which seems to suggest it was Mr. Zecevic, but it was, in fact, me. I think it is pretty obvious from what is said, but nonetheless ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, did you say 128?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: 129, 230D1. We have it on our screens. Sir, this is a document of the CSB Doboj. It is the Department for Administrative, Legal, and Personnel Affairs. The date is the 24th of September, 1992. There's a list of the public security stations to which this document was sent. And then it is signed by chief of the department, we see his name and we see a signature. Can you tell us who this person is, who actually signed this document, and what is the purpose of the document?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document is from the CSB Doboj. It is signed by the chief of the Department for Administrative, Legal, and Personnel Affairs. It was signed by Slavko Paleksic, the man who was the chief at the time. This is an invitation to a working meeting within his own line of work. He is inviting the chiefs of such departments from all the public security stations involved, and he is providing them with the agenda. So this is along a specific line of work. Perhaps I could put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: While we're on the document, sir, could you tell us what your recollection is, if you do remember, this activity along specific lines of work, coming from the CSB Doboj and involving all the public security stations in the area, when did that actually start happening?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In certain segments, it started happening in the month of July 1992, but we can say that it fully started functioning in all segments; namely, the milicija, the Crime Investigation Service, the administrative legal department, the financial department. We can say that this started functioning in August.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I would like to tender this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Was the meeting held, Mr. Bjelosevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Do we need the document, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, if I don't think I need it, I would not have offered it, Your Honours. But I'm in your hands. We have the testimony, I agree, to that effect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I would have thought that the meeting would be the important point here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: We are still on 139, are we? Tab 139.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: 129. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Your Honours, the purpose of this document is to show exactly what I was -- what I asked the witness, about the actual start of the function of the CSB Doboj in relation to its SJBs on the lines of work, and that is -- that is the only purpose of -- of this document. No other purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, we have his testimony, which is sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand and appreciate. Thank you very much, Your Honours. [Interpretation] Can we show the witness 231D1. That is tab 131.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, this is a rather poor photocopy but it's the only one we have. It is a document of the CSB Doboj, the 24th of September, 1992. Again, it was submitted to public security stations 1 through 7, and what is typewritten at the bottom of the page is: "Chief of the Centre, Andrija Bjelosevic." There's a signature there as well. Can you please confirm whether this is, indeed, your document? Can you tell us whether the document was sent, this order? Also, could you tell us what was the reason why you sent this document and what it relates to? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document of the CSB Doboj. I signed it. It was sent to the public security stations. The objective of this document is to ask very specifically, once again, for regulations to be observed in respect of the criteria for the reserve police. In certain stations, there were some members of the reserve milicija who had not even done their military service, whose ability was therefore quite unreliable. Then this followed. What is being asked for is that these criteria be applied by all means and that such persons have to meet all the criteria required by specific clearance. That is to say, that persons who have a criminal record cannot be on the reserve police force, also persons against whom there were proceedings that were under way. There were several orders to this effect, and this is one of them, in order to cleanse the reserve milicija, as it were. There's a procedure which says what to do with those who do not meet the criteria for being members of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us something about bullet point 3 in this order.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a warning which says that if this order is not applied, people who have failed to apply it will be taken to task.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unless there are objections, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked. But I have a question of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit 1D508, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, I understand your answer to counsel's question initially when dealing with this document, that it was a reminder. But I'm wondering whether there was any specific incident which triggered the -- or which prompted you to re-issue -- to issue this order at this time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We had information that in some public security stations there was still members of the reserve police who did not meet the required criteria; those prescribed by the law and the instructive documents issued by the ministry. That was the reason to reinforce the message decisively and explicitly, and that's why the order was issued to implement the procedure to clean the reserve police force from those who had criminal records; in other words, who were not suitable for the police tasks and duties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown 250D1, tab 163.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, this is a dispatch. It bears the date 6 November 1992. In the right-hand corner, you will see that it says the Security Services Centre Doboj. It was send sent to the administration for police duties and assignments at the MUP headquarters. The typed up signature is that of Andrija Bjelosevic, but there's the word "for." Can you confirm that this is a document sent from your CSB? Was it sent under your authority, with your knowledge, and what does this document refer to?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a dispatch which was sent from the Security Services Centre in Doboj. It was sent to the administration for police duties and assignments, whereby we replied to a dispatch, or rather, an order issued by the minister under the date you can see here and -- dated 23 October 1992. I remember the contents or, rather, what that was all about. A ratio of the reserve police and the active police was established. If my memory serves me well, I believe that that ratio was 1:2, which means that in -- if in one police station there were 50 active police officers, there could also be a hundred reserve police offers at the most to make the ratio 1:2. In the territory or, rather, in the area of the Doboj CSB, we did that. And this was signed by the chief of the police department in the CSB Doboj, Mr. Mirko Blazanovic. That department was duty-bound to implement the minister's order. When the order was implemented, a dispatch was sent to the minister to confirm that his order had been carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unless there are objections, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The usual question, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I will remind you that there is already in the -- in the exhibits a number of documents and the orders from the ministry concerning this rationalisation of the active towards the reserve police ratio. And this document confirms that at the beginning of November this order was implemented in -- in the CSB Doboj territory. And I believe that this -- this information is important, first of all, because it shows that the order of the ministry is implemented and the time when it was implemented only, and actually showing the span of time from the -- from the first order and then consecutive orders until the implementation in the territory. That is why I think it's relevant for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, is there something special or peculiar about the span of time? It's an order from the 23rd of October, if I'm not wrong, and it's implemented in the -- in the first week of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I mean, it's a reorganisation. It's not something you do instantly. So it's not -- it's normal that it takes some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But the first order is -- the first order on this matter dates, if I -- if I correctly remember at this moment, but I can check at the break, it dates in May 1992. That is precisely the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So the purpose of tendering this document is to show that it took months before --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, and that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: -- implementing the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: -- the order from the ministry or the minister would take a certain amount of time because of the situation in the territory to be implemented according to the order. And may I add, it needed to be re -- re-ordered couple of times before it was implemented. Yes. That is precisely the reason.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... that's a speech and a comment. But, Your Honours, can I make it clear, our case is that the orders issued by Mico Stanisic were being implemented. I mean, so I'm not quite clear where this is getting us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D509, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 3 -- 38D1 at tab 136. 38D1.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, these are minutes of the Expanded Session of the Expert Advisory Board of the Ministry of the Interior held on the 3rd of October, 1992, in Bijeljina. Among those present, we see your name. Could you please look at the document, and can you confirm whether you, indeed, attended that meeting. What do you remember about discussions at that meeting? And can you also tell us whether any conclusions were reached at the end of the meeting?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember the meeting. It was, indeed, held. I attended the meeting. Subsequently, we were provided with the minutes. The prevailing issues at the meeting were the improving of the work discipline, the implementation of certain laws and regulations, and in that sense, at the end of the meeting, several conclusions or directives or guide-lines were passed. You can call them whatever, but the essence of the matter is the same. One of those issues was providing accommodation for the employees of the Ministry of the Interior. We also established rules or, rather, criteria which would be applied to dealing with the issue. A commission was set up at the ministry level, and subcommissions were to be set up in the territories of CSBs that would deal with the issue. It was pointed out that all the services of the state and public security services had to be linked up, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I am particularly interested in your comment regarding page 5 of the document, paragraphs 6, 7, and 11. 6, 7, and 11. You confirm that you attended the meeting, so I would like to invite your comment on these bullet points.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In paragraph 6, people put in charge of preparing the report on the work of the ministry in the third quarter. Tasks were assigned to the chiefs of administrations and the chiefs of centres to carry out the activity and prepare information in a timely manner. I believe that we did that and that we sent a report for this quarter. In bullet point 7, you can see that all administrations of the ministry were hereby tasked with informing, by dispatch, all the internal organisation units within their responsibility. That reporting along the lines of work had to be put in place and it had to function; that was one of the tasks. Further on, bullet point 11, you said, right? Here heads of administrations in the ministry were given full legal powers to organise the operation of their respective administrations along the lines of work they controlled. At the same time, they were made responsible. They had the powers but they also had full responsibility for the work of the staff along the lines of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that, at the meeting, you also discussed the setting up of departments of the special police brigade in the seat -- or, rather, the departments of that unit in the security centres in the territory?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The special police brigade already was fully operational. It had detachments on its strength, and some of the detachments already had their bases. I remember that the security situation was very complex, very critical, very complicated, and that is why it was decided that those detachments should be deployed across the territory and that they should have certain obligations. Or, in other words, chiefs of security centres had certain powers with regard to those detachments in respect of certain situations. In other words, they could engage those detachments. However, they were requested to inform the ministry and the brigade commander as urgently as possible about their engagement and that engagement had to be approved and confirmed by the brigade commander. In Doboj, there was the base or the seat of the 5th Detachment. That's where the unit was based. The 5th Detachment was based in Doboj. There was one in Banja Luka. And let me not going on enumerating their places of deployment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, the detachments that comprised part of the special police brigade and that were accommodated at certain Security Services Centre in the territory, who commanded over them?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The immediate command was the detachment commanders, and they were subordinated to the brigade commander. And they were also, in a certain fashion, related to the chiefs of the Security Services Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Who was, at the time, in 1992, the commander of the special police brigade?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, Milenko Karisik was the commander of the special police brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D510, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have P405. It's tab 235.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, I'll wait for you to find the document.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Before we comment on the document, let me ask you the following. The MUP inspectors from the headquarters, would they arrive for instructive visits in 1992? And do you remember how many times they arrived to the CSB in Doboj?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they came. I think it was sometime in the autumn, and it was about the line of work of the police, the crime service, and later on also the line of work of administrative affairs. I think they didn't coming together. I think that the inspectors in charge of the line of work of the police and the crime department arrived first.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you maybe remember how many times they came?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they came twice in that autumn of 1992, if I remember it correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Take a look at this document. Page 5 in Serbian contains the names of the inspectors who performed the instructive control, as well as their signatures. This document is dated 22nd of October, 1992. Do you remember that the inspectors arrived? Do you remember what was the topic of the discussion? And what do you know about this document?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they arrived. And it was precisely Nikola Milanovic, Ostoja Minic, and Radenko Vujicic who arrived in one such visit. If I remember it correctly, first, they had a meeting in the centre. Then they went to visit some of the stations in the field. And then based on their observations, they drafted this report. Yes, exactly. Here they list the stations that they visited. I think we received one copy of this report. And then after their tour, they briefed us about their observations in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Take a look at page 2, the third paragraph, beginning with the words, "In CSB Doboj ..." Can you comment on this, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember this correctly, there was a memo sent to certain places, among others, to the command of the Operations Group Doboj. It was a long time ago, and I can't remember precisely the content of this memo. There were similar such memos containing complaints. They would come to my desk in the centre. Some of them would only go to the operations group command, and some of them only to the ministry. Very often, some of these complaints would only be signed by combatants or police and would not contain any specific names. But in all such cases, we verified the allegations, and in this particular case, I cannot remember what it was about. I do remember that a memo was sent with the complaint.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you comment on page 5 of this document, the last two sentences in the first paragraph. The sentence beginning with: "It was established in the SJB Doboj ..."

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They found certain problems in the public security station Doboj, and here they say that the -- there was no criminal log, the KU log. They say that a deadline was agreed and that all the entries were supposed to be entered retroactively, based on the temporary log-books that should have been kept. Or, alternatively, this should have been done based on other documents. Yes, there were certain problems. We also pointed to those problems. When I say "we," I mean the inspectors in my centre. And here we can see that the inspectors who came from the headquarters, from the MUP, established that certain problems were ongoing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just one more thing about this document. Page 4 regarding the situation in Bosanski Samac, we see the mention of some decision by SAO Semberija and Majevica. Do you know what this is about, and can you comment on it? It's the third sentence in the paragraph pertaining to Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember this. I would like to remind you again that from April onwards, there was no communication and no contagious territory between Doboj and the public security station in Samac, and that's when the Crisis Staff appointed the chief of the public security station there. And the Crisis Staff, probably its president or somebody else, contacted the representatives of the organs of SAO Semberija and Majevica, and since this was a compact territory and there were no connections with Doboj, as far as I know, they requested the public security station in Samac -- or, more precisely, the whole municipality of Samac to be connected and included in that territory. However, when the situation changed and there was a territorial link between us, then this station, the public security station in Samac, continued to function as part of the CSB Doboj. Later on, I don't remember exactly when it was, there was a reorganisation, and this station ended up as part of the CSB Bijeljina. That was later on. In this period, it was still part of the CSB in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I now want to show you 1D52, tab 154.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: A small point, Mr. Zecevic. I think the answer is self-evident, but in the first part of your -- of the answer to your last question, I heard in the interpretation, and the transcript confirms it, but the witness is recorded as saying, "There is no communication and no contagious territory," and then later on he talks about communication. I assume he meant "contiguous."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I believe so, yes. I'm not sure -- I know the word "contiguous." So that's my problem. Otherwise I would confirm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: But please confirm it for the record that that is what he meant to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you, in your reply, Mr. Bjelosevic, when you were commenting on the previous document, you said: "I want to remind you that from April onwards, there was no communication and no ... territory between Doboj and the public security station in Samac, and that's when the Crisis Staff appointed the chief of the public security station there." You were describing the character of the territory in question. Could you explain that? There was no communication, and it was what kind of territory?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that there was no communication between Doboj and Samac. By this I mean telephones and telexes, and there was no contiguous territory. It was not possible to pass through, because the area of Modrica and Odzak was the area that cut off the communication between the two points.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You didn't understand me. I asked you about the character about the territory comprised by SAO Semberija and Majevica --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I think I understood. I think his answer is sufficient, Mr. Zecevic. Thank you, Mr. Bjelosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The following document is 1D52, 154.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is a document originating in the Ministry of the Interior, Crime Prevention Administration. Mandatory instructions. October 1992, Bijeljina. Mr. Bjelosevic, are you familiar with these instructions? Were they received in the Doboj CSB? Were your stations informed about this, and did you apply it in your work?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember this. This instruction defines the procedure to be followed when searching for persons and property, who is authorised to initiate such a search, how it should be broadcast, and I can tell you that this instruction was applied in practice. Yesterday we touched upon this subject, and I can tell you that it was done in accordance with this instruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's why I showed you this document. The following document is 241D1. I think it's 241D1. Just a moment. Tab 152. Yes, I have received a confirmation that it is 241D1. So this is a document originating from the Security Services Centre in Doboj. The date is the 27th of October, 1992. It was addressed to public security station. Your name is typed, and there's also a signature. Is this your document and what is it about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a document of the CSB Doboj. I signed it. It was sent out to the public security stations. The objective was to regulate the situation in terms of dealing with the then-Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. I remember that at one of the meetings, it was stated that public security stations were directly addressing the organs of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and that that is something that left a poor impression and was unacceptable. So that is what was requested then, and, later on, that's what I asked people on the ground to do. Namely, that they should only communicate through the administration of the ministry, that the following -- that the proper chain should be followed, and that it's the ministry that had the right to communicate that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I would just like to ask you for your comment, because you confirmed that this is your document. Would you please have a look at the last paragraph in this communication, in this document.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That public security stations in the territory of the centre should inform by dispatches the Crime Prevention Administration of any criminal reports that are filed. And from then onwards, I think that's the way it worked, both in terms of general crime and economic crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you just explain this to us? What is stated here is that they are obliged to inform by dispatch the Crime Prevention Administration of any criminal reports that are filed.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Does that pertain to the period up until then?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up until then. So that there would be proper records in the administration, so that they could have all of this information available and be in a position to use it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please describe to us what "general crime" means? What is included under "general crime"?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General crimes are property-related crimes, homicides, causing general danger to the public. Economic crime is singled out, and it has to do with certain crimes in the field of the economy, different kinds of embezzlement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I would like to have this document admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D511, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I see the time. However, I don't know what your instructions are in view of the next break. When should we take the next break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We may as well stick to the usual time and take it at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we will resume in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, your instruction from last Friday was that we discuss the scheduling, and I propose that we take the adjournment earlier with the witness so we can discuss it, five minutes prior to the end of today's session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, you may continue, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 213D1, tab 118. Your Honours, I have four documents about the same issue. Therefore, I would like to tender just one of them, whether -- whereas, I would like to show only -- just to show the others, just to display the dates when they were issued, and ask the witness to confirm their issuance for the record. I would not seek to tender all four documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: As you wish, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown the second page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The date is 1st September 1992. The signatory of the document is the chief of centre, Andrija Bjelosevic. It was sent to the Ministry of the Interior. And the subject is: Nominations for positions of chief and commander of Petrovo SJB.
