Could you please confirm that this document was issued by yourself, and can you please explain the underlying reasons for sending this document.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a document sent by the Security Services Centre Doboj. I, indeed, signed it. It was sent to the Ministry of the Interior of the Republika Srpska, and the subject is: Nominations for positions of chief and commander of the Petrovo SJB. We have already discussed the Petrovo SJB today. It was set up in the month of August 1992. And then, pursuant to the prescribed procedure, nominations had to be made for positions of chief and commander of the public security station. And you can see that that was, indeed, done. There are three names here as nominees for the chief of the SJB. There are also nominations for the position of commander. There are two candidates.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Bjelosevic, was this the first time that chief and commander were appointed in this public security station?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Why? What was the reason?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Petrovo SJB did not exist prior to that. It was a new municipality on the map, as we have already stated. Those were the first nominations that were sent to the minister, and the minister then issued a decision on the appointment of both the chief and the commander of the SJB. And if I remember it well, Slobodan Katanic was appointed as the chief of the SJB, and I'm not sure whether Savo Gojkovic was appointed as commander. I'm not sure, but I believe that that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unless there are objections, I would like to tender the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Could you show us, Mr. Zecevic, how this would assist?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document shown to the witness last week, at the beginning of my direct examination, was the order of the minister dated 15th of May, where he instructs for which posts the agreement or the -- the agreement by the minister is required, such as chief of the SJB or commander of the SJB. However, we had a number of examples in the -- in the case where this procedure was not followed. Now, this is the document which shows how it should have been done, and that is precisely the reason why I'm showing it, to show what -- what would be the proper procedure in accordance with the order of the minister from 15th of May which should have been followed. Now, I have a number of documents, as I said, four documents, which illustrate the time when this procedure was actually -- started to be followed, and I think it's -- therefore, it's relevant. This is just an illustration. This document is an illustration on -- of the procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: But reminding ourselves that this -- that we are engaged in a trial and there is an indictment, and that this is not a broad-ranging commission of inquiry into the events that would have happened over the relevant period, I still have some difficulty bringing this -- the contents of this document home to what we are about, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, as I said on previous occasion when Ms. Korner was -- was objecting to certain --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I'm not sure how far this is going, but if it is going to be a discussion about the evidence and comment, and, I would suggest, speeches, I think the witness ought to take his headphones off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bjelosevic, please remove your headphones for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the part of the indictment is -- as I said before, when Ms. Korner was objecting to one of the documents, the part of the indictment is the CSB Doboj. And as I -- as I said already, the -- the chief of the CSB Doboj is allegedly member of the joint criminal -- or alleged joint criminal enterprise as well as our clients. Now, what I'm -- what we are trying to show is when the CSB started to operate and whether it operated in accordance with the laws and the regulations which were valid at the time. If that is -- if that would be the case, I think then -- then -- then the argument for the Defence is, I believe, clear, and we believe it's relevant because of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And these nominations go to the issue of the regularity of the -- of the events, conformity of the events to the practice and the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and effective control, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Very well. Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D512, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] The following document I would like to show to the witness is 243D1, tab 155. Tab 155.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is another document issued by the Doboj CSB. The date is 30th October 1992. On page 2, you will see a signature. Could you please confirm whether this document was issued by yourself and, also, could you please tell us what the document is about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is another document issued by the Doboj CSB. It was addressed to the Ministry of the Interior. This a proposal for the appointment of commanders in the SJB Maglaj in the territory of the Serbian Municipality of Maglaj. That SJB had already functioned from before, and the people nominated had already held those positions. However, the minister had to issue his decision on appointment. Previously, it was I who appointed them, in keeping with the minister's authorisation from the month of May 1992. The document was signed by myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you seek confirmation by this document?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. At the end of the document, you can see an explanation where it says that they are responsible, that they had proven responsible in their previous work.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What is the date of the document? When was it sent?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 30th of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The following document is 244D1, tab 156.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with this document. This is another proposal for appointment of chief of the Modrica SJB. Mr. Popovic was first appointed by the Crisis Staff of the municipality in Modrica, and when the Security Services Centre started operating in Doboj, I accepted this person as a chief who was very responsible and professional in the performance of his duties. Mr. Popovic was the secretary of the SUP even before the war, and that was one of the very rare occasions where a person was very loyal to his job, very professional, and that such a person had been appointed by the Crisis Staff to such a position. Obviously I didn't change my mind later, and I proposed that his appointment be confirmed by the minister. I signed the document, and the document was, indeed, sent on the date indicated herein.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What date was that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on the 30th of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown 269D1, tab 190.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tab 190. This document was issued by the Doboj CSB. The date is 29 November 1992. It was sent to the Ministry of the Interior, to the Administration for Legal Affairs and Personnel. The signatory is Andrija Bjelosevic, the chief of the centre. Can you confirm for us whether this is, indeed, your document, and what is it about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This document was issued by the Doboj Security Services Centre and the date when it was sent is indicated here. I signed it. There's a difference in date here. When I say "in date," I mean in respect of the proposals that had been sent prior to this one. Let me explain. The Crisis Staff at one point in time, when the Derventa SJB was established, appointed Dragoljub Kukic as the chief of the SJB. It also appointed Dusko Jovanovic as the commander of the SJB, and those two men did not have any prior experience working with the organs of the interior. Mr. Kukic had been a member of the Territorial Defence Staff and a National Defence Secretariat. And I wanted Mr. Slobodan Bilic to be appointed as the chief of the SJB. My original proposal featured his name. His name is not here, but it's neither here nor there. However, in the last paragraph of this document, there is a reference to his name because I say you must render invalid the decision of the appointment of Slobodan Bilic as chief of the Derventa SJB because, in the meantime, Mr. Bilic had turned down the position. And while this was going on, negotiations had to take place, and then a proposal was for the candidates as you can see them in this document. This explains why this proposal was sent somewhat later than the previous ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have now 242D1, tab 153.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is also the Doboj CSB, 27th of October, 1992, signed Chief of Centre, Andrija Bjelosevic. Can you confirm that this is your document? And can you tell us what is it about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a document originating in the Security Services Centre in Doboj, as dated here. I signed the document. It's a request for clearance. There was a candidate that I wanted to nominate for the position of the commander of the Doboj traffic safety police station. Since it was, so to speak, a civilian person, or, more precisely, he was member of the military at the time, and he was supposed to be appointed at a rather serious position in the MUP, we requested checks to be made. The outcome was positive, and Mr. Maric was appointed the commander of the Doboj traffic safety police station. Today, he is the chief of the CSB Doboj, which means that he remained working for the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I still have three or four documents relating to security checks and clearances. I propose to tender one of them for illustration purposes only through this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 288D1, tab 213.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is a document originating from the Security Services Centre in Doboj. On the fifth page, we can see the signature, Chief of Centre, Andrija Bjelosevic. The date is 20th of December, 1992. Subject: Verification request. And it's addressed to the National Security Service. Can you confirm this document and explain what it is about.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a document originating from the Security Services Centre in Doboj. I signed it. It's a request for verification, in relation to the members of the Security Service. Those people were assigned to various stations, and our request was granted. I can't remember the details. I don't know what the exact outcome of this verification was for each of those persons, but we did receive the information that we requested.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is this about appointment to some managerial positions or, generally speaking, is this about appointing somebody to work in Security Service in Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is about positions of authorised persons. Here you have two commanders, one assistant commander, policemen, inspector, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I propose to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D513, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, I would now like you to take a look at P1270, tab 228. Thank you. Sir, this is record of the extended meeting of the collegium of ministers held in Bijeljina on the 5th of November, 1992. We have here the list of the persons present. Can you confirm that you were present there, and can you remember the contents of this meeting? It's 228.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's a longer document.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us move to another document, and I'm going to double-check in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 252D1, 164.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is -- oh, excuse me. This is a document originating from the Doboj Security Services Centre, dated 9th of November, 1992, signed Chief of Centre, Andrija Bjelosevic. Can you confirm this, and can you explain the document?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember this document. A collegium was held on the 5th of November. Among other issues, there were various questions, comments, and discussion about the fact that certain public security stations were contacting the ministry directly and not through the CSB. It was concluded that this is detrimental to the system of management and the principle of subordination. And all the public security stations in the territory of the centre were sent a dispatch, telling them to adjust their work according to the conclusions accepted at the collegium because, otherwise, their observations and comments will not be take into consideration if they don't go through the CSB.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What is the situation with the internal regulations of the MUP? What is the normal procedure for communications within the ministry? Is it always necessary to communicate through the Security Services Centre?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to remind you that there was such a thing as instruction on briefing and reporting. There were some situations, and it was not unusual, when a certain station would report through a direct line. However, at the same time, they had the obligation to send the same dispatch to the Security Services Centre, because if they didn't, they would go against the rules and regulations. Maybe you remember, at the beginning of my testimony I mentioned that at the end of 1991 and at the beginning of 1992, this parallel reporting became a practice within the Ministry of Interior of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. If you remember, I highlighted this negative practice. However, it had already been established as a working practice. And here can you see that similar things were observed, and this issue was discussed at the collegium meeting with the minister present, and the conclusion was that the hierarchy should not be changed and that communications had to follow the usual channels.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My associates copied this tab 228 that you were unable to find. So, this is a record of the extended meeting of the collegium held on the 5th of November, 1992, in Bijeljina. Can you confirm that you were present at this meeting, and can you tell us what was the topic of discussion?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was present at this collegium meeting. A moment ago, I explained one of the conclusions taken at the collegium. The agenda of this meeting was rather long. As you can see, we discussed various proposals for rules, laws, et cetera, because the Ministry of Interior was supposed to comment on the proposals and put forward their suggestions. When we talk about laws, when we talk about rule-books, they were adopted by the minister himself, but it would always be preceded by a discussion so that various suggestions and proposals could be put forward. Yes, I remember this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether there was any discussion at this meeting about the regulations on disciplinary measures in the state of imminent threat of war?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that all documents that were discussed are enumerated here, beginning with the regulations on internal organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. I would like you to comment on page 5, the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Page 5?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assume that it's page 6 in e-court in English. Excuse me, it's page 7 in English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This concerns the area of the Trebinje CSB. It was confirmed for some of those municipalities that they fell under the authority of that centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, do you remember discussions about some issues or problems involving the Trebinje centre and the public security stations listed in here?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were problems. I believe that there was another meeting at which the then-chief spoke about those issues. A position was put up for the functions of the CSB to involve some of those stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, was the territorial organisation subsequently changed, in terms of those public security stations?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a later period, the situation did change. Some centres were reformed. I am not able to give you the precise date, but I know that the Foca Security Services Centre was set up and another one was set up in Prijedor. I really can't remember when that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just one more question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are on a good page in e-court in English. However, in the Serbian, I would like to call up page 6, paragraph number 1, which is the last paragraph in the English version on the page that we see on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, do you remember the issue which is raised here and mentioned in the minutes?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that that was pointed out as a problem in the functioning of the Zvornik SJB. The problem was that certain information was not forwarded either to the centre or the MUP. I don't know if my memory serves me well, but I believe that the problem involved a paramilitary unit. I believe that was something that was discussed at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bjelosevic, in the territory of your own centre, did you have similar situations or omissions, as it were? What I mean is this: Did the chiefs of SJBs in your territory fail to inform you about certain security events and situations?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did have such situations. We have already talked about that today and yesterday. We spoke about requests for information about certain vehicles. I have to point out that, on one occasion, at the Doboj SJB, there was a discussion about what needed to be forwarded to the centre -- or, rather, what the centre requested. The discussion became very heated. I was informed about that from some person who -- persons who had attended the meeting. One of the commanding officers said, and I quote, "From here the information leaks into the centre," which is beyond reason. This is not about leaking information. This is about sending information as to what was going on in the territory of each of the stations. We had certain problems with regard to information from the Samac public security station.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since we have raised that issue, could the witness please be shown 538D1, tab 169.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bjelosevic, that document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours. I'm getting tired so I started forgetting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bjelosevic, the document was issued on 13 November 1992. It is a decision to remand in custody assigned by Captain First Class Dragomir Majstorovic [as interpreted], I believe.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mestorovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Keserovic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Keserovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this case? What can you tell us about it?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Before Mr. Zecevic continues, I think we ought to note that there is an error in the translation of the date. I think it is pretty clear although -- well, not pretty clear, but clear that it is actually, as Mr. Zecevic says, the 13th of November, but it has been typed as the 31st of January, 1992. So somebody has reversed the numerals and then put in the wrong month.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Ms. Korner, I'm talking about the document 169, and it's all over 13th of November. I don't see anywhere --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, I don't have the translation. Should I have it? Should I be aware of the mistake?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Witness doesn't have the translations. Maybe we can --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... all I'm pointing out for your purposes, as this is your document, I think, that --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understood that it's just the intervention by the witness because he's not getting any translation. That's the only reason --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, I see. I thought he hadn't got the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I appreciate your help, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I have it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Okay. So, this document will be sent for revision of translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bjelosevic, did you hear my question? My question was this: Are you familiar with this case? What can you tell us about it? What do you remember about it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with this case. At that time, pursuant to an order by the commander of Doboj OG, I discharged duties as a battalion commander in the Teslic front line. But I was informed about this event. Commander Lisica gave me his approval to go and see what the case was about, and to return once the problem was resolved. Actually, in the territory of Samac, certain conflicts broke out because the military security organs, while performing their activities, established or received information that there had been some illegal activities on the part of certain officers in the military and that the then-station chief, Mr. Todorovic, was involved in those illegal activities. When those men were arrested, and Todorovic was one of them, the leadership of the municipality ordered the blocking of the corridor, or, rather, the road that passed through the corridor. That was the only passable road at the time. After I got abreast of the situation over the telephone, when I arrived in Doboj, it was then-commander of the public security station, Mr. Savo Cancarevic, who put me in the picture. I ordered the police not to get involved in the blockade. I sent an inspector from the police department, together with a number of men, police officers, to go down there and to re-establish order in that police station and to bring the police station back to its normal functioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: MFI'd until the revised translation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thanks, yes. I forgot that. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit 1D514, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 254D1, tab 171.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this dispatch bears the date 14 November. It was sent to the Republika Srpska MUP. Your name is typed up. The document also bears a number. Could you please confirm whether this dispatch was one of yours or not, and also what is the subject of this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a dispatch which I sent to inform the minister himself about what had happened in the territory of Samac at the time. There's also a quote in the document. I quoted the same information we were provided with at the centre. And I promised that I would monitor the situation after having dispatched my men down there, and I promised that I would report to the minister accordingly. This is the content of the dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In this dispatch, you also quote the dispatch that you, yourself, had received from Samac, and the signatory of that dispatch was Sekulic, Stoko, the public security station commander. Is it true that that person was, indeed, the commander of the station?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he was the deputy of the station commander. I knew Savo Cancarevic better, and I wanted to get in touch with him personally over the phone, and then he provided me all the details of what had happened. And as you can see, in the first part of my dispatch, I provide my report or, rather, a description of what I had learned, and in the second part, I forward the contents of the original dispatch that I had received from Samac, bearing the signature of the deputy commander, Stoko Sekulic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unless there are objections, I would like to tender the document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D515, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 255D1, tab 172.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is another dispatch sent by the Doboj CSB. This one was sent on the following day, on the 15th November. It was sent to the Republika Srpska MUP. In here, you forward a new dispatch with an explanation provided by the Samac SJB. You are the signatory, or, rather, your name is typed up at the bottom of the dispatch. Can you confirm whether this was, indeed, was your dispatch, and what do you know about the contents thereof? Could you also comment on the explanation that the deputy commander provided in his dispatch.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a dispatch from the Doboj CSB. I signed it, and I forwarded it. Several details are provided in here with regard to the procedure of the president of the War Presidency, where you see that he addressed the commanding officers in the SJB directly, and he asked them to participate in the obstruction of the road passing through the corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D516, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 257D1. It's tab 174.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, this is a dispatch dated 15th of November, sent to the president of the Presidency of Republika Srpska, as well as to the RS MUP. It is signed by Chief of Centre, Andrija Bjelosevic. Is it your dispatch, and can you explain it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a dispatch from the Doboj Security Services Centre that I sent, both to the president of the republic at the time and the other addressee, because this incident involved politics as well. You can see it if you read the dispatch. These were very serious matters. It had to do with the interference in work of the military and the public security station, and the goal was to release the persons arrested by the military. I considered this a serious issue. The assessment was that there may have -- that much bigger incidents may have occurred, that weapons may have been used, and that is why I wanted the president to be appraised of the situation and to help in resolving this situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I propose to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D517, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 263D1. It's tab 183.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, yesterday you spoke about the fact that sometime during that summer - I think it was August - you met Blagoje Simic, in relation to the work of the public security station in Samac. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you just briefly remind us of the topic and tell us why you went there to discuss it.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the inspectors from the Doboj public -- Doboj Security Services Centre inspected the public security station in Samac, they found a number of irregularities and concluded that the work was not at a satisfactory level. That is why I, together with the chief of the public security sector, and I also think the chief of the state security sector, went to Samac. I wanted to talk to the then-president of the War Presidency, Blagoje Simic. Why? It was the Crisis Staff who had appointed Stevan Todorovic on the position of the chief of the public security station, and the president of the Crisis Staff was Blagoje Simic. When I told him the reasons for our arrival, he was very curt, very impolite. He kept saying, Where were you back in April when we had to fight a war? We appointed him, and he is going to remain the president of the public security station. He also complained to me personally. He didn't like the fact that the state security inspectors visited the area of Odzak, and he told me that they should take care about what they were doing because they could end up in much worse situation than in Teslic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you suggest at that meeting then Stevan Todorovic should be replaced?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is exactly what I proposed, and as soon as I mentioned that, all normal communication between us ceased.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you now take a look at the document on the screen. The date is 25th of November. It's a dispatch sent to the Republika Srpska MUP in Bijeljina, to the minister. It's signed Chief of Centre, Andrija Bjelosevic. The text has been typed with two different typewriters. Can you explain that, and can you confirm that this is your document?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a document originating from the Doboj Security Services Centre. It's a dispatch sent to the minister. I signed it. But when the document reached me, I was of the opinion that I had to add something. I wanted to explain how Todorovic was appointed, and that was typewritten on the typewriter of my secretary, and after this was added, the dispatch was sent to the communications centre to be forwarded to the minister. At that moment, I thought it was possible to replace the chief, Todorovic, among other things, because the president of the republic was informed of his behaviour, and I thought that it could be done in this way.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will now show you the following document, 264D1, tab number 184. I would like you to confirm that this is the document identical to the previous one.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's the same text. The same text that we saw in the previous document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did this text reach the minister of the MUP of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to tender this document. Excuse me, I would like to tender this document, 264D1, tab 184.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The last one, I assume?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the last one because those are identical documents, the one witness explained why --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: -- there was a difference in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D518, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Don't forget the time, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. This is, I think, appropriate moment that we adjourn for the day, because we need to discuss the scheduling another five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, we are about to adjourn for the day, but we have some procedural matters with which to deal. So, again, you are excused from the court before we rise. The Usher will see you out. Thank you. We would resume tomorrow morning at 9.00 in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, having spent 16 hours, we are informed at this point, could you perhaps begin by indicating where you see and how you see the -- your -- your dealings with this witness continuing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I indicated at the beginning that I would need 20 hours, but I think I would -- I would be able to finish by second break tomorrow, which means one hour less than estimated. But, of course, it would depend on the situation. I mean, that is about the time that I'm needing for the rest of the documents that I want to show to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You realise, Mr. Zecevic, that there are still 120 documents to go. In 16 hours, you showed 150 documents, more or less, and there are still -- no, a little bit more. And there are still 160 to go. So you are a little bit over halfway.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I know, Your Honours, but I have selected documents. I wasn't really sure which of the documents from the list I would use, so for that -- for this purpose, and in order to bring the -- the most important and the relevant document, I had to cut short on some others which are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And you already know how many documents you still have to show?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I have them here. I think it's 30, 32 documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But I would not like to limit myself to that number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So, in sum, we can safely conclude that your examination-in-chief and Mr. Krgovic's cross-examination of this witness would be finished within the eight sitting hours remaining in this week.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, definitely, Your Honours, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Any comments, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... considering the position. I understood that Mr. Krgovic's cross-examination was going to last about hour and a half. Is that still the estimate? So if Mr. Zecevic finishes round about the second break tomorrow, Mr. Krgovic is likely to trickle into Thursday. Right. I have a few questions I want to ask the witness before he goes back. I don't want to start my cross-examination proper but there are some matters that I wish to deal with before he goes. In particular, in relation to documents. So, in any event, there is no conceivable way that I could conclude what is now likely to be a far extended cross-examination in the light of the evidence that has been led from this witness by the break. The question then remains, Your Honours, when is he to return? I suggested that we still had the three days of next week free, but I didn't hear a response to that. I don't know whether there was any response. But, again, I'm not certain I could conclude my cross-examination then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Perhaps counsel can speak outside of court, and if they have further thoughts on this matter, you would let us know at some point between tomorrow and Thursday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Your Honour, it is quite obvious I can't, not in a million years, even scratch the surface of a cross-examination [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Oh, we understand that. I'm talking about in terms of next week.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Your Honours, the --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's really --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: To assist you in your discussions, there are any number of reasons why sitting next week may not be feasible so --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, in that case, Your Honour, I mean, there's no point. If Your Honours are unable to deal -- or the Court is unable to deal with it next week, well, then that's the end of that. Your Honours, we've discussed with -- Mr. Zecevic and I have discussed when he should come back. Mr. Zecevic would wish to still call the two experts for the allotted period, that is from the 2nd of May through to approximately, I think, the 20th of May, and Mr. Bjelosevic to return after that. We have no objection to that. We know the problems that Mr. Zecevic has with his experts. It's a question of Your Honours, if you're happy to defer cross-examination until after the experts. Your Honours, I should add, of course, that the document list we gave to the Defence is now so out of date that we're going to have to re-do the whole thing, so, in any event, they will be getting a brand new document list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. So we take the adjournment to tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 20th day of April, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.
